corpus_note: Questions from the hackathon synthetic pack (EN + Pidgin verified). Answers are team drafts: dateless, procedural, and unverified against official INEC publications. Do not rely on them without official review.
source_note: Draft answer. Verify against the current official INEC publication before relying on it.

faqs.a_en: Use only the official INEC voter verification channel for your election to check your registration status. Do not trust forwarded links; type official addresses yourself or use contacts published by INEC.

q.en: How do I check if I am registered to vote?
q.pcm: How I fit check say I don register to vote?

faqs.a_en: Registration requirements are published officially by INEC for each registration exercise. Check the current official INEC notice before visiting a centre.

q.en: What documents do I need to register?
q.pcm: Wetin I go carry to register?

faqs.a_en: PVC collection points and schedules are announced officially by INEC, usually at local government or registration area level. Confirm the current collection notice from an official INEC channel before going.

q.en: How do I collect my Permanent Voter Card (PVC)?
q.pcm: How I go take my PVC?

faqs.a_en: INEC announces an official procedure for lost or damaged cards before each election cycle. Check the current official INEC notice, and do not pay anyone who claims they can reprint your card.

q.en: What if my PVC is lost or damaged?
q.pcm: Wetin I go do if my PVC loss or spoil?

faqs.a_en: No. You need your Permanent Voter Card to be accredited and to vote. Anyone telling you otherwise is misleading you.

q.en: Can I vote without a PVC?
q.pcm: I fit vote if I no get PVC?

faqs.a_en: Opening and closing times are set officially for each election. Confirm the official INEC announcement for your election and ignore forwarded messages claiming changes.

q.en: What time do polling units open and close?
q.pcm: Wetin be the time wey polling unit dey open and close?

faqs.a_en: Your polling unit is assigned at registration and shown on your card and voter slip. Confirm it through the official INEC voter verification channel before election day.

q.en: How do I find my polling unit?
q.pcm: How I go find my polling unit?

faqs.a_en: Do not photograph your marked ballot. Ballot secrecy protects you, and violating it can be an electoral offence.

q.en: Can I take a photo of my ballot?
q.pcm: I fit take photo of my ballot paper?

faqs.a_en: Support measures for voters with disabilities are published by INEC and observer groups for each election. Ask officials at your polling unit on arrival, and report barriers through official observation channels.

q.en: What support exists for voters with disabilities?
q.pcm: Wetin dey for people wey get disability to vote?

faqs.a_en: Yes. A voter who cannot see or read may be assisted by a person of their choice, following the official procedure explained by polling officials. Your helper must follow your instructions.

q.en: Can someone assist me to vote if I cannot see or read?
q.pcm: Person fit help me vote if I no fit see or read?

faqs.a_en: Results are collated and announced through the official INEC process, from polling units upward. Only announcements from official INEC channels count; figures circulating on social media are unverified.

q.en: How are results announced?
q.pcm: How dem dey announce results?

faqs.a_en: Only the returning officer duly designated under the electoral law can declare the official result for an election. Any other declaration is not official.

q.en: Who can declare the official election result?
q.pcm: Who fit declare the official result?

faqs.a_en: Report vote buying or intimidation to INEC officials, security agencies, or accredited observer hotlines, with the location, time, and what happened. Do not confront offenders yourself.

q.en: How do I report vote buying or intimidation?
q.pcm: How I go report say dem dey buy vote or dey threaten people?

faqs.a_en: Yes. Your vote is secret. Nobody is entitled to see your marked ballot or know how you voted.

q.en: Is my vote secret?
q.pcm: Na secret my vote be?

faqs.a_en: Check whether the message appears on an official INEC channel. Be suspicious of forwarded broadcasts with no source, urgent threats, or exaggerated claims; verify before sharing.

q.en: How can I tell if a viral election message is fake?
q.pcm: How I fit know say viral election message na fake?

faqs.a_en: Use official INEC channels and recognised fact-checking organisations. Treat viral forwards as unverified until confirmed there.

q.en: Where can I find official election information?
q.pcm: Where I fit see correct election information?

faqs.a_en: Only persons and organisations duly accredited as observers may observe. Accreditation details are published officially by INEC.

q.en: Who is allowed to observe an election?
q.pcm: Who fit observe election?

faqs.a_en: Voters already in the queue at the official closing time are normally allowed to vote. Follow the instructions of polling officials at your unit.

q.en: What happens if I am in the queue when polls close?
q.pcm: Wetin go happen if I dey queue when polling close?

faqs.a_en: Transfer windows and procedures are announced officially by INEC. Check the current official notice for whether transfers are open and where to apply.

q.en: Can I transfer my registration to a new location?
q.pcm: I fit move my registration go new place?

faqs.a_en: No. You vote at the polling unit where you are registered. If you have moved, check the official INEC notice on transfers before the deadline.

q.en: Can I vote if I am outside my state?
q.pcm: I fit vote if I no dey my state?
